intact mental status? (baseline vs chg)

ETOH & drug use
Seizure:
michigan law for driving: seizure free x 6M -can only ‘advise pt’
DOCUMENT
electrical activity for partial/focal seizure: amount of neurons firing simultaneously + which area of brain
HPI              1st time vs recurrent? Freq -is it ↑?      -1st time = major wrk up
witnessed vs unwitnessed: trauma, timing, typical Sx    -Hx from family, EMS, etc
Hx seizures: congenital/genetic/anatomic/structural/metabolic/acquired/idiopathic
Triggers: flashing lights, loud noises/music, strong emotions, gaming-stim
relationship of seizure to other events: stressors
Abnorm lyte, ETOH use or w/draw?
Seizure meds: anticonvulsants (taking as Rx’d?)
Meds that ↓seizure threshold: TCA, wellbutrin, opioids, antipsych, fluoroquinolones, penicillins, carbapenems, stimulants, anesthetics (lidocaine)
pre seizure aura: staring, smells (burning), numbness/tingling, sudden fear/anxiety, deja vu, N/V, dizzy
automatism: eyelid fluttering, chewing, lip smacking, swallowing, guttural sounds (focal), tongue biting or
incontinence: intra-oral lacerations (generalized, tonic-clonic)
post ictal period (time to return to baseline awareness/function)? Behavior?: typical Sx/S or duration?
secondary trauma or injury: ex. Injury during seizure, injury precipitating seizure
muscle tone (loss of)
ROS
tumor   -    infection    -    hydrocephalus   -    meds    -    trauma
Causes
: VITAMINS
Vascular: strokes, bleeds
Infectious: meningitis, encephalitis, brain abscess
traumatic/toxic: head injury, penetrating trauma (GSW), EtOH, cocaine -focal irritation
Autoimmune: CNS vasculitis, lupus
Metabolic (esp for 1st time): lytes, glucose, hyperthyroid, hepatic or uremic encephalopathy
Idiopathic: Epilepsy
Neoplasm: irritation, structural chgs
Syncope, Psychogenic, other ddx
seizure types
focal w retained or impaired awareness (simple focal)                                         Post-ictal period: shorter
MC Location: 1 part of motor cortex                    **extent of motor cortex involved = severity**
Severity: aura -to- generalized (simple focal seizure Sx)
generalized tonic-clonic (grand mal or major motor)                                             Post-ictal period: longer
Sx/S: LOC & muscle tone -> rhythmic overall muscle contraction
Fall out of bed/chair, tongue biting, Incontinence
red flags: 1st seizure   -   prolonged post-ictal state    -  incomplete recovery of neuro deficits    -   2ndry injury
todd's paralysis:
brief, transient paralysis following a seizure
status epilepticus:
life threatening: hypoxia & autonomic instability
single/back-to-back tonic clonic -persist for 5min OR successive seizures w/o return to baseline alertness
tx: IV benzos (rectal if no IV access & pt actively seizing), airway support, antiseizure meds
**********Only red flags to hsp**********
Other HPI

HPI              onset: sudden/progressive     -    quality: burning, sharp, etc     -     intensity       -    impact on ADLs  & QOL
assoc manifestations                -    Location                                      -     meds             -    efforts to treat
Gait
HPI:    -      assoc dx: arthritis, stroke, seizure     -   new meds?    -    falling, balance   -    gait chg: ortho/neuro/both?
Tremor
HPI              upper vs lower extremities? Both?                    -    onset: sudden or gradual                     -     meds
character: worse w rest, intentional mvt          -    relieved by: rest, activity, alcohol       -    assoc problems
Assoc Dx: Hyperthyroidism      -    familial tremor      -    liver or kidney dx      -    ETOH use      -     MS
assoc meds:     neuroleptics (antipsych)                -   valproate, phenytoin          -    caffeine
Albuterol     -   corticosteroids      -    pseudoephedrine              -     antiarrhythmias
types of tremors
Resting tremor: present at rest, ↓w voluntary mvt (4–6 Hz)
Causes: Parkinson’s disease (MCC), drug-induced parkinsonism (neuroleptics, metoclopramide), Wilson’s disease
Intention (action) tremor: worsens as limb approaches a target; absent at rest
Causes: cerebellar disease or damage (MS, cerebellar stroke, chronic ETOH, spinocerebellar ataxias), phenytoin or valproate toxicity
Essential/postural tremor: occurs w sustained posture or action; relieved by rest or sm amount of ETOH

Causes: essential (familial) tremor (MCC of action tremor), hyperthyroidism, meds (albuterol, corticosteroids, caffeine, pseudoephedrine, valproate, lithium), anxiety, physiologic (exertion, caffeine)
Asterixis (“liver flap”): hand-flapping tremor on wrist dorsiflexion; NOT a true tremor
Causes: metabolic encephalopathy (hepatic, uremic, CO2 retention), toxic/medication causes
Weakness
HPI              location: proximal/distal/symmetric/asymmetric                        -       onset
character: generalized/localized                                                      -     Meds: HIV anti-virals, amphotericin B
concurrent chronic illness: HIV, nutritional or ↓B12                   -    Weakness vs fatigue? Both?
Acute weakness or numbness suggests: vascular event (CVA vs TIA)      -     assoc Sx/S
Numbness
ROS:            central vs peripheral nerve dysfunction: where -map on dermatome
metabolic: thyroid, hypocalcemia, hyperventilation
acute weakness or numbness suggests: vascular event (CVA vs TIA)
Dizziness
woozy? lightheaded? spinning sensation? -hallpike maneuver
Vertigo: sensation of mvt when none
Positional?
HA
loss of function    -   fever    -   wake pt from sleep    -   unremitting   -   Hx CA w poss met potential to brain
Red Flags:
severe (worst HA of my life)    -     extremes of age    -     trauma     -     IS: atypical encephalitis meningitis
radical change of HA from baseline presentation: freq, level of pain, palliative chgs
acute mental status/behavior changes: esp when family says deviation
sudden loss of function
Causes:  vasc event   -  CNS/PNS trauma    -  intoxication    -  drug OD   -    drug: side effect, toxicity, w/draw, 5HT syndrome
loss or sudden change in Level of consciousness
Causes:       Seizure      -    Trauma      -   delirium      -  ↓BG      -   drug OD      -   intracranial process: CVA, tumor, trauma, bleed
cerebral hypoperfusion: dysrhythmia, bradycardia, hypovolemia, orthostasis, aortic stenosis
Anatomy
Brain Bleed
Brain blood supply = 20% CO
arterial supply: 2 internal carotids & 2 vertebral
venous drainage: venous plexuses + dural sinuses & 2 internal jugular veins
places blood can accumulate: epidural space     -     subdural space     -     subarachnoid space
Complications of brain bleed: ischemia -relieve P by burr hole
acute weakness or numbness suggests: vascular event (CVA vs TIA)
